# Verdict: REVISE ## Summary The `Modal` component demonstrates a thoughtful initial foundation—implementing `role="dialog"`, `aria-modal="true"`, `aria-labelledby`, an Escape key listener, and focus restoration to the opening trigger. However, two **MAJOR** architectural design gaps compromise assistive technology navigation and focus containment: (1) rendering into a portal without applying `inert` or `aria-hidden="true"` to background siblings leaves the background DOM exposed to screen reader virtual cursors (VoiceOver/TalkBack/JAWS browse mode); and (2) the custom `FOCUSABLE_SELECTOR` omits native interactive elements like `` and fails to account for `
` or `visibility: hidden`, causing focus trap escapes. Several minor implementation gaps (`type="button"` omission, exposed symbol character, and rigid initial focus) must also be addressed before shipping. --- ### Pre-commitment Predictions Before inspecting the fixture code, five common modal dialog design gaps were predicted: 1. *Focus trap absent or failing on reverse tab (Shift+Tab).* -> **Partially confirmed:** Trap logic exists, but the query selector misses key elements like `` and mishandles `
`. 2. *Focus restoration fails or restores to document body.* -> **Partially confirmed:** Implemented, but lacks a fallback if the trigger element unmounts during the modal's lifecycle. 3. *Screen reader virtual cursor can escape into background content.* -> **Confirmed:** Portal mounts directly to `document.body` without setting `inert` or `aria-hidden` on background siblings. 4. *Initial focus lands abruptly on close button, skipping title/description.* -> **Confirmed:** In the DOM, `modal-close` precedes `children`, so initial focus always lands on "Close dialog", skipping body content. 5. *Missing `aria-describedby` or accessible name calculation issues.* -> **Confirmed:** `aria-describedby` is absent, and the close button symbol `✕` is exposed without `aria-hidden="true"`. --- ## Findings ### Critical Findings (blocks access) *No critical blockers identified. Basic keyboard tab containment and Escape key dismissal function on standard form elements.* --- ### Major Findings (significantly degrades experience) #### 1. Background Content Exposed to Screen Reader Virtual Cursor (`inert` Missing on Siblings) - **Evidence**: `Modal.jsx:124-148` (`ReactDOM.createPortal(..., document.body)`) and `Modal.jsx:68-113` (`handleTabKey` only traps the `Tab` key). - **User Group Impacted**: Screen reader users (especially Safari + VoiceOver, iOS VoiceOver, TalkBack, and NVDA/JAWS in browse mode). - **WCAG / APG Citation**: WCAG 2.4.3 Focus Order (Level A), WCAG 1.3.2 Meaningful Sequence (Level A), WAI-ARIA APG Dialog (Modal) Pattern. - **Why This Matters**: While `handleTabKey` traps Tab navigation for keyboard users, screen reader users navigate primarily via reading keys (swipe gestures or Up/Down virtual cursor). `aria-modal="true"` is not consistently honored across all browser and screen reader combinations (notably WebKit/VoiceOver). Because the modal is portaled into `document.body` without marking sibling nodes (such as `
`) as `inert` or `aria-hidden="true"`, screen reader users can navigate directly out of the modal dialog into background page content, landmarks, and inputs. - **Fix**: Apply the HTML `inert` attribute (or `aria-hidden="true"`) to background sibling elements when the modal opens, and remove it on unmount. Alternatively, use a portal container structure where background application nodes are isolated and inerted. - **Confidence**: HIGH ``` ### A11y Evidence Finding finding_id: modal_background_not_inert fingerprint: b8c19d42e0f711ad source: Modal.jsx:124 wcag_or_apg: WCAG 2.4.3 Focus Order (Level A), WAI-ARIA APG Dialog (Modal) section_508_fpc_context: not in scope severity: MAJOR perspective_alarms: screen_reader=HIGH, keyboard=LOW evidence: ReactDOM.createPortal(
...
, document.body) lacks inert management for sibling DOM nodes. reproduction_steps: 1. Open modal in Safari with VoiceOver enabled. 2. Navigate using VO + Left/Right arrows past the modal boundary. 3. Observe cursor entering main page landmarks and links behind the overlay. expected_behavior: Assistive technology virtual cursor must be constrained within the modal dialog boundaries while open. actual_behavior: Virtual cursor navigates through inert background DOM content. trend: new ``` #### 2. Incomplete Focusable Selector and `visibility: hidden` Edge Case in Focus Trap - **Evidence**: `Modal.jsx:6-17` (`FOCUSABLE_SELECTOR`) and `Modal.jsx:20-24` (`getFocusableElements`). - **User Group Impacted**: Keyboard-only users. - **WCAG / APG Citation**: WCAG 2.1.1 Keyboard (Level A), WCAG 2.1.2 No Keyboard Trap (Level A). - **Why This Matters**: 1. `` (inside `
`), `iframe`, and SVG links (`svg a[href]`) are natively keyboard-focusable but omitted from `FOCUSABLE_SELECTOR`. If `` is the last focusable element in `children`, `handleTabKey` does not recognize it as `lastElement`. When tabbing from ``, `handleTabKey` executes no trap logic, and focus escapes the modal into the browser chrome or background. 2. `button:not([disabled])` matches buttons inside a `
`. Native HTML disables buttons inside disabled fieldsets; including them in the focusable array can cause focus calls to fail or miscalculate boundary elements. 3. `el.getClientRects().length > 0` filters out `display: none`, but does **not** filter out `visibility: hidden` (which maintains geometry and generates client rects). Elements styled with `visibility: hidden` are included in `focusableElements`, causing focus to stall on an invisible element. - **Fix**: Update `FOCUSABLE_SELECTOR` to include `summary`, `iframe`, and `svg a[href]`; exclude elements inside disabled fieldsets (`:not(fieldset[disabled] *)`); and verify computed visibility (`window.getComputedStyle(el).visibility !== 'hidden'`). - **Confidence**: HIGH --- ### Minor Findings (friction but workaround exists) #### 1. Close Button Missing Explicit `type="button"` - **Evidence**: `Modal.jsx:138-143`: ``. - **User Group Impacted**: Keyboard and screen reader users interacting with embedded forms. - **WCAG / APG Citation**: WCAG 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value (Level A). - **Why This Matters**: In HTML, buttons default to `type="submit"`. If `Modal` wraps a `
` or is rendered inside one, pressing Enter or clicking the close button triggers form submission rather than clean dismissal. - **Fix**: Explicitly add `type="button"` to the close button. #### 2. Visual Symbol Character `✕` Not Hidden from Assistive Technology - **Evidence**: `Modal.jsx:142`: `✕`. - **User Group Impacted**: Screen reader users and speech-input (Voice Control) users. - **WCAG / APG Citation**: WCAG 1.1.1 Non-text Content (Level A), WCAG 2.5.3 Label in Name (Level A). - **Why This Matters**: Although `aria-label="Close dialog"` supplies the accessible name, speech synthesis engines and braille displays can verbalize the raw Unicode symbol (e.g., "Close dialog button, multiplication x"). Furthermore, speech-to-text users visually see "✕" and may issue commands like "click cross" or "click times" which fail to match "Close dialog". - **Fix**: Wrap `✕` in `✕`. #### 3. Initial Focus Rigidly Set on Close Button; Container Lacks Fallback `tabindex="-1"` - **Evidence**: `Modal.jsx:41-45`: ```javascript const firstFocusable = getFocusableElements(modalRef.current)[0]; firstFocusable?.focus(); ``` and `Modal.css:14`: `.modal-dialog:focus { outline: 3px solid #0066cc; outline-offset: 2px; }`. - **User Group Impacted**: Screen reader and keyboard users. - **WCAG / APG Citation**: WAI-ARIA APG Dialog (Modal) Pattern, WCAG 2.4.3 Focus Order (Level A). - **Why This Matters**: Because `modal-header` precedes `modal-body` in the DOM, `firstFocusable` is always `button.modal-close`. A screen reader user immediately hears "Close dialog, button", skipping the modal body content entirely until they manually navigate backward or forward. Furthermore, if `children` contains no focusable elements, `firstFocusable` is `undefined`, leaving focus in the background. Note that CSS defines `.modal-dialog:focus`, but `.modal-dialog` lacks `tabindex="-1"`. - **Fix**: Add `tabindex="-1"` to `.modal-dialog`. Provide an option to focus the first input or primary action in `modal-body`, with fallback focus directed to `.modal-dialog`. #### 4. Focus Restoration Lost if Opening Trigger Element Is Removed - **Evidence**: `Modal.jsx:49-51`: `previouslyFocusedElement.current?.focus();`. - **User Group Impacted**: Keyboard and screen reader users. - **WCAG / APG Citation**: WCAG 2.4.3 Focus Order (Level A). - **Why This Matters**: In common modal patterns like "Delete Item" confirmations, the button that opened the modal is deleted from the DOM upon confirmation. When the modal unmounts, calling `.focus()` on the disconnected node fails silently, resetting focus to `document.body`. - **Fix**: Verify `document.body.contains(previouslyFocusedElement.current)` before restoring focus; if disconnected, fall back to an appropriate container, main landmark, or the parent list. --- ### Enhancements (best practice not met) 1. **Add `aria-describedby` Prop Support**: - `Modal.jsx:131-136` provides `aria-labelledby="modal-title"`, but offers no `aria-describedby` linking to a description ID in `modal-body`. Adding an optional `descriptionId` prop ensures screen readers announce the modal's summary when opened. 2. **Close Button Minimum Touch Target**: - CSS lines 30-38 set `font-size: 24px; padding: 4px 8px;`. The target size computes to ~32x32 CSS pixels. While this meets WCAG 2.2 AA SC 2.5.8 (24x24 px), increasing padding to achieve at least 44x44 CSS pixels satisfies WCAG AAA SC 2.5.5 and mobile touch target recommendations. 3. **Scrollable Region Keyboard Operability**: - `.modal-dialog` has `max-height: 80vh; overflow-y: auto;`. Adding `tabindex="-1"` (or `tabindex="0"` when scrollable without internal focusable elements) ensures keyboard-only users can scroll long content with arrow/page keys (WCAG 2.1.1). --- ### What's Missing - **Background Inertness Mechanism**: No mechanism to mark background content `inert` when the portal mounts. - **Initial Focus Customization**: No `initialFocusRef` prop allowing dialogs with forms or confirmations to direct initial focus to the first field or confirmation button rather than the close button. - **Trigger Disconnection Fallback**: No fallback target if `previouslyFocusedElement` has been removed from the DOM. - **Description Association**: No `aria-describedby` wiring for introductory text in the modal body. --- ### Multi-Perspective Notes - **Screen Reader User**: - The dialog name is communicated via `aria-labelledby="modal-title"`. - *Gap*: Because siblings are not inert, virtual cursor users can wander out of the modal into background page content. Initial focus lands on the close button, so users hear "Close dialog button" before hearing the modal content. - **Keyboard-only User**: - Escape closes the modal, Tab wraps properly between standard controls, and focus restores to the trigger on close. - *Gap*: The focus trap breaks if the modal contains `` elements or controls inside disabled fieldsets. - **Low Vision User (200% Zoom, High Contrast)**: - Focus outlines on `.modal-close:focus` and `.modal-dialog:focus` use `#0066cc`, which provides a 5.58:1 contrast ratio against white (exceeding WCAG 2.4.13 3:1 requirements). - *Consideration*: At 200% zoom, `max-height: 80vh` with `overflow-y: auto` causes vertical scrolling; ensure the scroll container itself can receive focus to scroll via keyboard. - **Cognitive Accessibility**: - Escape key handling and backdrop click dismissal are predictable and standard. --- ### Perspective Alarm Levels | Perspective | Alarm Level | Trigger Signal | | :--- | :---: | :--- | | **Screen reader** | **HIGH** | Portal lacking `inert` on siblings allows virtual cursor escape; initial focus bypasses body content. | | **Keyboard-only** | **MEDIUM** | Focus trap selector omits `` and mishandles `
`. | | **Low vision** | **LOW** | Outline contrast is 5.58:1 (passes 3:1); dialog reflows with internal scroll. | | **Cognitive** | **LOW** | Clear title, explicit close button, predictable Escape key dismissal. | | **Vestibular & motion** | **LOW** | No animations or transitions beyond a subtle color hover. | | **Auditory access** | **LOW** | No media elements or audio notifications present in the shell. | | **Environmental contrast**| **LOW** | `#333` text on white is 12.6:1; `#666` close button is 5.74:1 (passes 4.5:1). | --- ### Verdict Justification **Verdict: REVISE** While this component gets several core accessibility patterns right (proper ARIA role and label, Escape listener, and Tab trap logic), it cannot be accepted as-is: 1. The absence of `inert` on background siblings allows screen reader virtual cursors to escape the dialog into the rest of the application. 2. The focus trap's element selector omits common focusable elements (``) and includes disabled controls within disabled fieldsets, which causes focus leakage or trap stalls. 3. The close button lacks `type="button"` and initial focus management is overly rigid. Addressing these findings will upgrade the verdict to **ACCEPT**. --- ### Open Questions (unscored) 1. *Does the host application have a single root container (e.g., `
`)?* If so, applying `inert` to `#root` while `isOpen` is true is trivial and solves the virtual cursor escape issue cleanly. 2. *Will this modal host long-form reading content or confirmation flows?* If long-form, initial focus should be directed to `.modal-dialog` (`tabindex="-1"`) rather than the close button.
